claims.text: The proposed approach combines high-throughput ab initio phonon calculations with machine-learning-based environment descriptors.
The hybrid approach will predict and identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity HEAs more accurately than current state-of-the-art methods.
The approach will improve predictive precision by approximately 15–25%.
The approach will be accurate over 300–800 K.
The intended materials are single-phase or near-single-phase HEAs with relatively uniform microstructures and little secondary-phase precipitation.
The model can meaningfully capture local chemical and vibrational disorder across multi-principal-element alloy compositions.
HEA lattices exhibit atomistic disorder and force-constant fluctuations associated with their multielement environments.
Atomistic disorder and force-constant fluctuations strongly affect phonon scattering in HEAs.
Ab initio phonon data can quantify intrinsic sources of phonon scattering relevant to thermal conductivity.
Machine-learning descriptors can capture short-range ordering and chemical complexity in HEAs.
Combining ab initio information with machine learning enables a more robust assessment of phonon heat conduction.
The framework will accurately screen HEAs whose lattice thermal conductivity is below 2 W/(m·K).
Existing ab initio or rudimentary scattering models inadequately represent configurational and vibrational disorder in multi-principal-element alloys.
Inadequate disorder representations cause existing methods to underestimate or overestimate phonon-scattering effects.
The model may be inaccurate for alloys with substantial secondary phases, extreme-temperature exposure, or heavily defected microstructures outside its training domain.
The magnitude of improvement may vary with alloy chemistry and processing history because comprehensive composition-space data are limited.

The hypothesis is defined as falsified if more than half of measured lattice thermal conductivities deviate from the hybrid model's predictions by more than 25% across the tested compositions and temperature range.
